notes: Both supplied verbs are italicized in the ASV; the ruling rests on the absence of any verb morpheme in either colon (rules 20 and 7), and the ASV's own rendered material stands between them, so they are two `added` units (rule 2).

*hasteth* echoes the lexeme of the participle אָץ, and reading it as a second discontinuous realization of that morpheme under rules 25 and 34 was the competing analysis. It was rejected on rule 34's subtraction test: אָץ keeps its whole rendering in *one that is hasty*, so what *hasteth* adds is a predication the Hebrew never wrote for that colon.
*tend* was read the same way rather than as rule 20's linking-verb copula, since it supplies a predication of its own beside a prepositional phrase that already holds *only to plenteousness*.
